name: Distribution board plan mark
summary: Plan mark showing the position of a distribution board or consumer unit on an installation layout.
description: On installation plans a distribution board is drawn as a rectangle against the wall, typically half filled or crossed, with its designation such as DB-1 written beside it. Home-run arrows from outlets and lights terminate in labels that refer back to this board.

The mark tells the reader where circuits originate and where the board schedule applies. In domestic work the same form is used for a consumer unit, often labelled CU. Clearance in front of the board and access requirements should be checked against the architectural plan.
The plan mark does not show the internal arrangement. The board schedule and single-line diagram show incoming supply, protective devices and circuits.
readingNotes: Read the designation and look up the board schedule.
distinction: A switchboard object on a GA shows a physical lineup; the plan mark only locates a board on a building plan.
